newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Co-op rejects Lanica deal.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Co-op rejects Lanica deal.

text.p: Britain's Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS) on Monday rejected the attentions of Lanica Trust Plc, saying there was no chance it might sell some its operations to the investment group, led by Andrew Regan.
British newspapers have reported that Lanica is interested in buying CWS's non-food businesses such as banking and funeral operations.

But the co-operative made it clear no such deal was on the cards. "The board will not be bullied by Lanica or anybody else into parting with businesses," chairman Len Fyfe said, while announcing lower full-year profits.
Pre-tax profit for the year to January 11 fell to 54.1 million pounds from 64.1 million due to fierce competition in food markets.

"Last year brought mixed results and significant change within CWS. We are aiming for an improved performance from our activities and are confident that, under new executive leadership and following a wide ranging business review, this will be delivered," Fyfe said.

Shares in Lanica, which are currently suspended, surged last year on speculation that Regan was seeking to acquire operations from the Co-op, which distributes profits to its members. It has food stores as well as other operations such as banking and funerals.

Graham Melmoth, chief executive, said in a statement, "Over the years, CWS has proved to be a durable and democratic institution in its implementation of the co-operative ideal. It is ironic therefore that we should attract the hostile attention of Lanica, which is controlled by a small group of Monte Carlo-based millionaires.
He added CWS would not sell assets to an "asset-stripping middleman".

"Lanica is an insubstantial company which has been suspended from listing for over two months. Given its background, I cannot envisage the circumstances in which it would be in the interests of our members to deal with Lanica. It is questionable whether it will now ever be requoted," Melmoth added.
